problem: What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola $5{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}=20?$

feedback.problem:
Complete the following parametric equations generating the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{12}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{7}=1$ in terms of the parameter $t,$ defined for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ]$ where $t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.$

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡t$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

In our case, $a=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}$ and $b=\sqrt{7}.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=\sqrt{7}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$
